title: Synthesis of Functionalized 10-nm Polymer-coated Gold Particles for Endothelium Targeting and Drug Delivery
protocol: Prepare a 1 M sodium hydroxide (NaOH) stock solution by dissolving 400 mg NaOH in 10 mL ultrapure water and mixing well.
Dissolve 2.4 g of NaOH in 10 mL of ultrapure water to prepare a 6M NaOH stock solution.
Store the 6M NaOH stock solution at room temperature.
Prepare a 250 mM chloroauric acid (HAuCl4) stock solution by dissolving 1 g of dried HAuCl4 in 10.16 mL of ultrapure water.
Dilute 1 mL of the 250 mM HAuCl4 with 9 mL of ultrapure water to obtain a working concentration of 25 mM HAuCl4.
Store the 25 mM HAuCl4 solution at room temperature.
Prepare a 0.1 M carbonate buffer at pH 8.8 by dissolving 84 mg sodium bicarbonate in 10 mL of ultrapure water.
Adjust the pH to 8.8 by adding 6 M NaOH from step 1.2 as needed.
Store the 0.1 M carbonate buffer at room temperature.
Mix 20 mL of tetrazolium compound with phenazine ethosulfate (PES).
Store the MTS/PES mixture in aliquots at -20°C in dark.
Add 12 µL of 80% THPC in water to 1 mL of water in a microcentrifuge tube.
Pour 45 mL of water into a 100-mL round bottom flask and stir with a magnetic stir bar at 300 rpm.
Add 0.5 mL of 1 M NaOH and 1 mL of diluted THPC solution to the stirring mixture.
Stir the reaction vigorously for 5 min.
Add 2 mL of 25 mM HAuCl4 solution to the mixture.
Continue stirring for an additional 15 min to allow complete formation of gold cores.
Dissolve 30 mg NH2-PEG-SH in 1 mL water in a glass vial.
Dissolve 7.5 mg m-PEG-SH in 1 mL water in a separate glass vial.
Dissolve 7.5 mg COOH-PEG-SH in 1 mL water in another glass vial.
Reduce stirring speed of the solution in the round bottom flask to 100 rpm.
Add PEG solutions to the THPC capped AuNPs dropwise while gently stirring.
Stir the mixture overnight at room temperature.
Prepare a 4 L bucket of water and stir it at 60 rpm.
Use a 12-14 kDa molecular weight cutoff cellulose membrane for dialysis.
Tie the ends of the dialysis membranes using clips.
Transfer the solution into the dialysis membrane via pipette.
Change the water every 2 hours for the first 6 hours.
Change the water every 6 to 12 hours for the remaining 66 hours.
Filter the semi-purified nanoparticle solution through a 0.2 µm syringe filter into a 50-mL conical tube.
Place the conical tube in a -80 °C freezer.
Allow the purified PEGylated AuNP (PEG-AuNP) solution to freeze for about 5 h.
Use a freeze dryer to lyophilize the purified PEG-AuNP.
Store the dry, purified PEG-AuNP at 4 °C until use.
Secure a 50-mL round bottom flask over the center of a magnetic stir plate.
Fill the flask with 18 mL of water.
Stir the water at 100 rpm using an egg-shaped magnetic stir bar.
Weigh 2 mg of lyophilized PEG-AuNP in a 4 mL conical tube.
Use an anti-static gun to eliminate static charge and clinging of the PEG-AuNP powder to the tube surface.
Add 2 mL of water to the tube.
Pour the 2 mL PEG-AuNP solution into the round bottom flask for further reconstitution in a total of 20 mL of water.
Continue to stir the mixture at 100 rpm using an egg-shaped magnetic stir bar.
Add 1 mL of 0.1 M, pH 8.8 carbonate buffer to the 20 mL of reconstituted AuNP contained in the round bottom flask.
Continue stirring.
Add 5 µL of 10 mg/mL fluorescent NHS ester in dimethyl sulfoxide.
Stir the fluorescent PEG overnight at room temperature and covered in foil.
Dialyze the stirred mixture using a 4 L bucket of water and a 12-14 kDa molecular weight cutoff cellulose membrane.
Change the water every 2 hours for the first 6 hours.
Change the water every 6 to 12 hours for the remaining 66 hours.
Obtain 1 mL of the purified fluorescent PEG-AuNP solution for characterization.
Freeze and lyophilize the remaining solution to obtain fluorescent nanoparticles in powdered form.
Store the powder at 4°C.
Reconstitute the stored powder with a 0.2 µm syringe filter to sterilize and remove any potential precipitates.
Drop 10 μL of the purified fluorescent PEG-AuNP solution onto a carbon coated mesh TEM grid.
After 5 minutes, use a piece of filter paper to carefully wick away excess liquid from the edge of the TEM grid.
View the fluorescent PEG-AuNPs at 80 kV and at a magnification of 50,000-150,000.
Take digital pictures of the fluorescent PEG-AuNPs.
Transfer 1 mg of lyophilized THPC-coated AuNPs into a microcentrifuge tube.
Transfer 1 mg of lyophilized PEG-AuNP in a separate tube.
Add 1 mL of water to each tube and transfer each AuNP solution to a 1 mL clear plastic cuvette.
Place the AuNP solutions in a DLS instrument and measure spherical hydrodynamic diameters using particle analyzer software.
Plot the measured hydrodynamic diameters using a histogram format.
Remove the cuvette from the DLS and insert into a spectrofluorometer.
Set the excitation wavelength to 633 nm and read emitted fluorescence signals along a wavelength range of 650-800 nm.
Confirm that the peak is approximately 665 nm.
Adjust the excitation and emission wavelengths according to the fluorophore used.
Pipette 100 µL of DMEM into each well of a 96-well clear bottom sterile tissue culture treated plate.
Add 3.2 x 10^3 cells to each well containing DMEM.
Allow the cells to grow to confluency in humidity and 5% CO2 controlled incubators at 37 °C.
Prepare individual microcentrifuge tubes, each containing 300 µL of DMEM with nanoparticles of various concentrations.
Aspirate the DMEM from the tube.
Fill the wells in triplicate with 100 µL of DMEM media containing 0, 10, 50, 100, 250, 500, or 1,000 µg/mL of AuNP.
Allow the cells and nanoparticles to co-incubate for a pre-determined length of time, here for 16 h.
Thaw the MTS/PES mixture from step 1.5.
Incubate the cells.
Aspirate DMEM and suspended nanoparticles from the wells.
Add 100 µL of fresh DMEM to each well.
Add 20 µL of MTS/PES solution to obtain a 1:5 ratio with DMEM.
Incubate the cells with MTS/PES at 37 °C for 2 h.
Perform colorimetric analysis by reading absorbance at 492 nm.
Calculate the average absorbance from triplicate values.
Divide the average absorbance by the control value from wells without nanoparticles.
Seed 1.0 x 104 cells/cm2 rat fat pad endothelial cells onto sterile 12 mm glass coverslips.
Feed cells with DMEM supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% penicillin/streptomycin.
Allow the cells to grow to full confluency in humidity and CO2 controlled incubators at 37 °C for approximately 3 days.
Add treatments to modify the glycocalyx, if applicable.
Treat cultured endothelial cells with 2.5 x 10-6 IU heparinase III enzyme for 2 h to degrade the glycocalyx by specifically cleaving its heparan sulfate component.
Incubate the endothelial cells with fluorescent AuNPs at 550 µg/mL for 16 h or other desired time.
Gently wash the cells with 2 mL of 37 °C 1% bovine serum albumin in phosphate buffered saline (PBS; containing 100 mg/L calcium and 100 mg/L magnesium).
Submerge the cells in 2 mL of 2% paraformaldehyde and 0.1% glutaraldehyde in PBS.
Allow the cells to fix for 30 min at room temperature.
Remove the aldehyde fixing solution and wash the cells with room temperature PBS for three 5-min cycles.
Expose endothelial cells to 2% goat serum in PBS for 30 min at room temperature to block non-specific binding sites.
Incubate endothelial cells overnight with 1% anti-heparan sulfate primary antibody in 2% goat serum in PBS at 4 °C.
Ensure that fixed cells are fully in contact with the antibody solution.
Wash out the antibody with room temperature PBS for three 10 min cycles.
Incubate the endothelial cells with a 1:1,000 dilution of the appropriate fluorescent secondary antibody for 30 min at room temperature, in the dark or covered with aluminum foil.
Wash out the secondary antibody with room temperature PBS for three 10 min cycles.
Mount the coverslip onto microscope slides using an anti-fade mounting medium containing DAPI for nuclei staining.
Seal the edges of the coverslip using nail polish.

Image the fluorescent immunostained endothelial cell samples with confocal microscopy, using blue, green, and far red channels to visualize the nuclei, heparan sulfate glycocalyx, and nanoparticles respectively.
